Good morning, Rafael. This is Claire Miller, from the legal team in Chicago. Thank you for opening the data room yesterday. We have started the due diligence, and we have three requests. First, could you provide the tax documents for the last five years? We only found three. Second, would you be able to send us a list of all active lawsuits? Third, we noticed that one supplier contract is not signed. We would appreciate it if you could explain that by Friday. Thank you, and have a good day.

In twenty years of mergers and acquisitions, I have learned one simple thing about due diligence. The buyer is not looking for a perfect company. The buyer is looking for surprises. A small problem that you disclose early is a detail. The same problem, found later in the data room, is a red flag. So my advice to sellers is this. Be organized, be fast, and be honest. Answer every request in writing. If you cannot send a document today, say when you will send it. And never hide a liability. The buyer will find it, and then the price will change, or the deal will end.

First, thank the buyer for the meeting. Then, confirm what is already in the data room. Next, listen to each request and ask for clarification if needed. After that, say when you will send each document. Finally, disclose any problem early and in writing.
